extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, narratologists, and advanced creative-writing students
extracted.subtask_description: Analyze and control a narrative's temporal aspects (sequence, duration, frequency, and aspect) with attention to iterative vs. singulative modes, their alternations, transitions, and the effects of memory and narrating on temporal order. Useful for critics analyzing modernist fiction and writers aiming to shape temporal experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel treatment of internal and external diachronies
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the internal (psychological/memory) and external (story-world) diachronies in an approximately parallel way thanks to a skillful arrangement of episodes, without necessarily departing from the base frequentative tense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use episode arrangement so memory-time and event-time mirror one another when desired. Example: Proust maintains frequentative base tense while aligning internal/external diachronies. Anti-pattern: random episode order that breaks parallelism and confuses temporal relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the iterative as a developmental mode (iterative plateaux)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop relationships and long-term changes by iterative plateaux marked by adverbials like 'thenceforth', 'since', 'now', treating stories as successions of states rather than causal event-chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor iterative constructions to synthesize repeated states and to convey stagnation or habitual perception (e.g., love developing as repeated states). Anti-pattern: forcing linear causal narration where the intended effect is the static/iterative sense of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative as expression of memory's masking of continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit the iterative aspect to show characters' incapacity to perceive continuity: memory reduces temporal distance by substituting repeated states for diachronic progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use iterative narration to dramatize forgetting or the inability to reconstitute past situations. Example: Marcel unable to measure the distance between past and present. Scoring note: effective when it thematically aligns with character psychology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternation of iterative and singulative as primary rhythmic principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the narrative rhythm not as alternating summary and scene (classical model) but as alternation between iterative (habitual/general) and singulative (specific/eventive) modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan large-scale rhythm around iterative/singulative alternation. Anti-pattern: expecting scene/summary alternation to accomplish effects intended for iterative/singulative shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional subordinations between iterative and singulative sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize complex structures where an iterative section can be subordinated to a singulative scene (and vice versa), producing relations like illustration, explanation, or insertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map iterative sections as background/explanatory material and singulative scenes as illustrative moments (or invert). Example patterns: iterative-within-scene; singulative-within-iterative; nested subordinations producing complex effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding unresolved aspectual transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the narrative indicates the temporal standing of a singulative relative to a preceding iterative (or vice versa); failing to do so causes the narrative to pass from one aspect to another without assignable relation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit temporal markers (e.g., 'once', 'the first of these days') or syntactic cues to prevent 'floating' scenes. Anti-pattern: sequences that seem to make a habit simultaneously a singular event, producing irreducible unrealism or 'floating' impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting and handling pseudo-iterative and aberrant past forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Be alert to pseudo-iterative constructions and aberrant uses of the simple past (passe simple) that can create the impression of careless or incoherent temporal handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such forms appear, consider textual variants or authorial revision before ascribing error. Example: Vigneron's hypothesis of 'whitewashing with imperfects' vs. textual correction in later edition. Anti-pattern: attributing all ambiguity to editorial mishap without textual comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret tense/aspect in context (imperfect as concomitance vs. iterative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Read imperfect-forms in context: imperfects may be concomitant/durative (singulative descriptive) or iterative (habitual); adverbials like 'suddenly' can force a non-durative reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lexical cues (adverbs, temporal phrases) and surrounding verb-forms to disambiguate aspect. Example: 'Tout à coup le ciel se déchirait' vs corrected 'se déchira' alters aspectual reading. Scoring: clarity of aspectual intent improves reader comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use corrections/variants to resolve ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that authorial or editorial revisions can change aspectual readings—textual variants may resolve or generate temporal ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare editions/variants when diagnosing temporal incoherence. Example: 1913 vs 1917 versions of Proust. Anti-pattern: treating every ambiguous passage as error rather than potential deliberate modulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masking transitions with neutral/ambiguous sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpose neutral sections to prevent readers from noticing aspect changes; three types: present-tense discursive excursuses, abruptive dialogue (without declarative verb), and ambiguous imperfect sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral sections deliberately to smooth transitions; be aware they may also hide confusion. Examples: present-tense excursus in La Prisonniere; abruptive dialogue in Sainte-Euverte conversation; ambiguous imperfects between iterative and singulative passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abruptive dialogue as aspect-neutral transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ dialogue without declarative verbs (abruptive dialogue) to create transitions that lack aspectual determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use abruptive exchanges to interrupt aspectual flow or to effect rapid shifts in focalization. Anti-pattern: overuse leading to reader disorientation when no other cues anchor time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous imperfects to sustain irresoluteness or modulate tonality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sequences of imperfects whose aspectual value remains indeterminate to sustain tonal or temporal ambiguity over extended passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skillful prolonged ambiguity can produce 'Wagnerian' continuous modulation; risk: reader confusion if ambiguity lacks artistic purpose. Example: long transition in Un amour de Swann.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative syllepsis as temporal condensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the iterative syllepsis to condense several events into a single narrative instance, thereby abolishing their succession and shrinking duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply iterative syllepsis to compress recurrent events into epochal statements. Note that iterative affects not only frequency but sequence and duration. Anti-pattern: accidental syllepsis that erases necessary causal or chronological distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations among analepsis, summary and iteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand that analepsis (flashback) often appears as summary, summary frequently uses iterative forms, and description tends to be pinpointed/durative/iterative—these categories interact and overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing or analyzing flashbacks, consider how summary/iteration will affect perceived duration and sequence. Scoring: coherence improves when these relations are systematically managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify temporal distortions: order, duration, frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize three main kinds of temporal distortion—interpolations (order/anachronies), distortions/ellipses (duration), and temporal condensations (frequency)—each alters a different temporal axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnose which axis is being manipulated to explain narrative effects. Example taxonomy: analepses = order; scenes/ellipses = duration; iterative syllepsis = frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify temporal manipulations by realism of lived or remembered experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground interpolations and distortions in plausible motivations: telling things as they were lived (existence's anachrony) or as they were recalled (memory's anachrony).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align temporal strategy with narrative voice: memory-driven narrators legitimately reorder events; present-tense reportage may require other justifications. Anti-pattern: arbitrary distortions without psychological or narrational rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish narrative temporality from narrating temporality
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate the temporality of the narrative (how story-time is represented) from the temporality of the narrating (the act of telling), since narrating can impose its own temporality (e.g., rushed denouements, overloaded final scenes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit when the act of narrating distorts story-time—excessive narrating-temporality can produce monstrous scenes and enormous ellipses. Critically evaluate whose temporal perspective governs each passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of temporal markers to anchor transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide temporal indications (e.g., 'once', 'the first of these days') to isolate an episode within a series and clarify its aspectual belonging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When moving from iterative to singulative or vice versa, add a marker to prevent ambiguity. Anti-pattern: leaving transitions unmarked, producing 'floating' episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate hesitation or absence of choice as a stylistic device
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an unresolved alternation between iterative and singulative—sometimes consciously chosen—to produce effects of patchwork, collage, or an emergent unity born retroactively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that deliberate indeterminacy can be aesthetic (Proustian 'unity after the event') but may also resist joining; weigh artistic aim against potential reader difficulty.
